items.title: NIO Stock Drops. The Weak Chinese Car Market Is Too Much to Overcome.
items.summary: The weak Chinese car market is too much for electric vehicle maker  NIO  to overcome.  Following earnings, Citi analyst Jeff Chung cut his sales estimates and price target to $7.10 from $8.20.  Declines left shares off 41% over the past 12 months.

items.title: GM's U.S. footprint for EV batteries has dwindled to 1 location
items.summary: Three years ago, GM had ownership stakes in four battery plants with two partners: South Korean companies LG Energy Solution and Samsung SDI.

items.title: How pickup trucks took centre stage with consumers and the U.S.-Canada trade war

items.title: Ford and GM Will Have to Pay Tariffs on Cars Made in Canada
items.summary: New Canada tariffs are landing as a direct bill to two of America's biggest automakers, and the ripple effects stretch well beyond car lots into the housing market and household budgets.

items.title: AT&T (T) Joins Skilled Trades Coalition Targeting 1 Million Workers By 2035
items.summary: AT&T (NYSE:T) joins the Lowe's Foundation as a founding corporate partner in the new Building Futures Skilled Trades Coalition. The coalition includes companies such as NVIDIA and General Motors and targets training and certification for 1 million skilled trades workers by 2035. The effort is aimed at addressing the U.S. skilled trade workforce gap that affects infrastructure projects and broader economic resilience. items.title: Lowe's launches major effort to help close America's skilled trades gap
items.summary: Lowe's Foundation launched a coalition with Nvidia, General Motors and over 75 partners to train and certify 1 million skilled tradespeople by 2035.

items.title: Why Toyota and Honda would get hit hardest by Trump's Canadian auto tariffs
items.summary: In something of an unexpected consequence, Japanese automakers Toyota and Honda have more to lose than any US automaker from President Trump's threatened tariffs on Canadian-built vehicles.
